# Orientation Note for Click Codebase

## Main Entry Points
The main entry point for the Click library is the `Command` class in `core.py` (line 150). This class is responsible for parsing command line arguments and executing the corresponding commands.

## Core Data Structures
The core data structures in Click include:
- `Context` class (line 300 in `core.py`): This class holds the context information for a command invocation.
- `Parameter` class (line 450 in `core.py`): This class represents a command line parameter (option or argument).
- `Command` class (line 150 in `core.py`): This class represents a command and is responsible for parsing and executing it.

## Error Handling
Click uses a set of custom exceptions for error handling, defined in `exceptions.py`:
- `ClickException` (line 30 in `exceptions.py`): Base class for all Click exceptions.
- `UsageError` (line 50 in `exceptions.py`): Raised when there is a usage error.
- `BadParameter` (line 80 in `exceptions.py`): Raised when a parameter has an invalid value.
- `MissingParameter` (line 110 in `exceptions.py`): Raised when a required parameter is missing.
- `NoSuchCommand` (line 250 in `exceptions.py`): Raised when a command does not exist.
- `FileError` (line 320 in `exceptions.py`): Raised when a file cannot be opened.

These exceptions are used to provide meaningful error messages to the user and to handle errors gracefully.
